review: 1:1–1:4 — the refrain بِحُبِّهِ opens three stanzas and then becomes the whole stanza's argument in the fourth; the Hebrew repeats בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ at the same place, because the repetition is the tune.
2:1–2:2 מִטִּיט הַחֲטָאִים הֱרִימָנִי — Psalm 40:3 (מִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן); the Arabic مِنْ حَمْأَةِ الذُّنُوبِ قَدْ رَفَعَنِي is that pit and that lifting, and טִיט is the psalm's word.
3:1 צְלָב גָּלְגָּלְתָּא — the Arabic الْجُلْجُثَه is the Aramaic place-name, kept as the Gospels keep it (Mark 15:22); the construct needs the Aramaic form rather than a translation.
4:1 נָפֹצוּ פַּחֲדַי — the Arabic مَخَاوِفِي تَبَدَّدَت is 'my fears were scattered'; נָפוֹץ is the biblical verb for scattering, and the plural construct keeps the personal possessor.

4:3–4:4 פּוֹתֵחַ שַׁעַר הָעֹנֶג / לְמַעַן אֶמְלֹךְ עִמּוֹ — the Arabic فَاتِحٌ بَابَ النَّعِيم / كَيْ أَمْلِكَ مَعهُ is Rev 3:21 (אֶתֵּן לוֹ לָשֶׁבֶת עִמִּי), and Hebrew keeps 'reign with Him' as the purpose clause.
